A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiffuGuard study. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on dLLM safety, defense effectiveness, utility, inference speed, component ablations, and hyperparameter sensitivity in Sections 3–5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds adaptive-attack experiments, analyses across additional models, and human and alternative-evaluator assessments in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The stochastic annealing remasking and block-level audit-and-repair procedures remain unchanged. Equations 7–10 and Algorithm 1 retain the same randomness schedule, Safety Divergence calculation, remasking, token suppression, and first-block repair.

E1.justification: Appendix D.3 adds defense-aware adversaries that optimize prompts to evade Safety Divergence detection, substantially extending the tested threat conditions. Table 11 also adds PAD evaluations on HarmBench prompts. The original datasets and four evaluated models remain; StrongREJECT is introduced as an assessment method.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds random-remasking and alpha=0.3 comparison rows for both LLaDA and Dream alongside the retained component ablations. Table 1 retains PPL-Filter and Self-reminder. The additional safety judges are evaluators, rather than new defense baselines.

E3.justification: New protocols include success across five temperature-varied attempts, SD-minimizing adversarial optimization, human assessment of 200 samples per dataset, additional classifier judges, and StrongREJECT scoring. Original settings in Tables 3–6 remain unchanged. V2's corrected description of transferred GCG agrees with v1 Appendix A.3 and does not establish a changed experiment.

E4.justification: Table 2 expands the ablation to remasking controls, AutoDAN, and GSM8K. Appendices D.3–D.5 add adaptive robustness tests, extend the motivating randomness and token-injection analyses beyond LLaDA, and examine evaluator dependence. Figure 4 additionally tests a compliance-token intervention on jailbreak queries. Existing sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix D.3 newly specifies five generation attempts per prompt at different temperatures, aggregated by whether any attempt succeeds. This adds repeated-sampling information for an attack protocol, without adding confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-seed uncertainty estimates for the existing results.

E6.justification: Table 1 remains unchanged, while expanded ablations and Tables 9–11 add substantial results. Table 9 reports threshold-probing ASRs of 65.58% and 84.62% for defended LLaDA and Dream. A new Table 2 AutoDAN entry is ambiguous: LLaDA+DiffuGuard scores 16.73%, whereas Table 1 reports 31.54% alone and 16.73% with Self-reminder. The unexplained configuration difference prevents interpreting this as a same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: The numbered equations and algorithmic mathematical definitions are retained. V2 adds explanatory threat-model and autoregressive-model discussion, but no new mathematical derivations, propositions, proofs, or formal guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, including the headline ASR reduction from 47.9% to 14.7%. The introduction and conclusion retain the same intra-step/inter-step findings, two-component training-free defense, and claims of preserved utility and efficiency.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 clarifies attacker and defender access and operational constraints. New Appendix F.3 acknowledges similarities with AR safety phenomena while explaining distinctions involving remasking, parallel decoding, and path dependence. Added experiments receive robustness and evaluator-agreement interpretations; the existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 specifies implementation details for the added experiments, including sampling temperatures, o3-mini, Llama-Guard-3-8B, HarmBench-Llama-2-13b-cls, and manual-evaluation sample counts. Existing checkpoints, hardware, precision, and principal hyperparameters remain unchanged. The new reproducibility statement repeats the code access already supplied in v1.

R1.justification: Appendix F.3 adds targeted positioning against prior AR decoding and shallow-alignment studies, including Huang et al., Zhang et al., and Qi et al. HarmBench, StrongREJECT, and several other references are added. The main related-work taxonomy and overall contribution positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence are largely retained. Local revisions clarify background notation, the threat model, and GCG categorization. V2 updates author and publication information, adds acknowledgments, reproducibility and LLM-usage statements, and renumbers appendices around the additions.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn, replacing its detailed method schematic with enlarged outcome displays. Figure 4 gains a bar, Figure 6 corrects swapped PAD/WildJailbreak labels, and Table 2 gains rows and columns. Three new tables and two multi-panel appendix figures present expanded evidence. The existing judge prompt is retained as Figure 11.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation by testing defense-aware attacks, checking the primary evaluator against human and alternative assessments, and extending the motivating analyses beyond LLaDA. These address important gaps in v1, while expanded ablations better establish component contributions and utility costs. The high adaptive ASRs warrant more cautious robustness claims, and some defense configurations remain unclear, but the added validation and evidence of failure conditions provide a substantial net improvement.
